w: During Swamishri's morning hours of personal consultation a youth came to see him. He had borrowed a large sum of money which he had loaned to four other people. The regular payment of interest money he got from them he paid it as interest money he owed to his loaner. Seeing there was no gain out of it, Swamishri asked him, "What do you get out of this!" Youth: "I get the same interest money that I pay to my loaner." Swamishri: "You must understand that your debt is not being paid at all! If the amount you have loaned to others doesn't come back then you will be in trouble. Pay back your loan and clear yourself of the debt." The youth realised his folly and promised to do what Swamishri had advised

During his evening blessings, Swamishri said, "Only through the Gunatit sadhu can we realise the knowledge of atma and Paramatma.. Through a person like Yogiji Maharaj one can learn Brahmvidya and be happy in this life and the life hereafter. By associating with a Gunatit sadhu, with a pure feeling that he is a God-communion sadhu, the giver of moksha, one who has no faults and who loves all - then only does one benefit abundantly."
Swamishri inaugurated a 4-day Eye-diagnostic camp organized by the local Bangalore Jain community.

Slated as Kishore Day, the evening assembly saw three dramas that showed death as being auspicious, steadfastness in one's vow and horizons of faith. The kishores held a 'niyam-tula' where they honored Lord Harikrishna Maharaj by weighing Him against their moral pledges. Finally Swamishri blessed the assembly.
At 8.55 am Swamishri left Amdavad to go to Sarangpur, arriving there at 11.00am.
Swamishri performed the inauguration ceremony for the relocated and newly built gaushala (cattle sheds) at Sarangpur.

At 5.25 pm, Swamishri left Sarangpur for Gadhada arriving for darshan at Lakshmi Vadi at 6.10 pm. Then, after visiting the Gopinath Dev Mandir for darshan, Swamishri arrived at the BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir on the hill.
Swamishri had a hectic schedule of visiting eight villages.

At 9.10 a.m., Swamishri departed from Navsari and arrived at Tankal at 9.35 a.m. Swamishri's car stopped on the outskirts of the village and observed the land donated for a Hari mandir. After giving flowers to be showered on the land to the devotees, Swamishri departed.
At 10.05 a.m., Swamishri arrived in Donja. Swamishri performed pujan and arti of the renovated Hari mandir dedicated for the women devotees. An assembly was held and Swamishri blessed the devotees.
At Sarvani-Vandarvela, Swamishri performed pujan and arti of murtis at the Hari mandir and then attended the Satsang assembly.
At 5.00 p.m., Swamishri departed from Sarvni-Vandarvela and stopped enroute to bless the devotees of Khudvel, Khambda and Golvad villages. At Chikhli Swamishri blessed a devotee.
At 6.00 p.m., Swamishri arrived at Bilimora. Swamishri perform pujan and arti at the Hari mandir and gave a discourse to devotees.
At 6.40 p.m., Swamishri arrived at Khaparvada. Swamishri performed arti and pujan of murtis in the Hari mandir. Swamishri blessed the assembly and departed at 7.40 p.m.
At 8.20 p.m., Swamishri arrived at the Swaminarayan Mandir in Kosamba (Tithal).

w: A satsangi youth from abroad showed Swamishri the plans for some mandirs. The youth and other volunteers were working extremely hard to accomplish the deadline given by Swamishri. With reference to this the youth echoed the burden of the project, “Swami, we simply don’t get enough time to rest or sleep.” Swamishri advised, “God is going to do everything. You just have to keep endeavoring. Remember God while working. He is the doer. Secondly, always say that it is going to be done but do not speak weakly. Thirdly, when you all get together to discuss, you must accept the result of what is decided in the meeting. Don’t criticize each other. Unity should be a priority.” Swamishri outlined the three principles of management, namely, God as the doer and personal effort, to speak in a spiritual manner but not weakly and to work unitedly.

pr.t: Power of Effort and Refuge in God
w: An unhappy aspirant expressed his woes, “There is no success in the business I’m running. I believe that many years ago someone had given me food that was illomened. When I was young my jealous aunt had given me something to eat that was charmed with bad mantras...” “What is your aunt doing now?” interrupted Swamishri. “She is dead,” replied the aspirant. “Then give up your thought about your aunt. What can she do to you now! Start putting in more effort in your business. Pray to God. Nobody had given you anything bad to eat. Give up the superstition you have. God is your protector. You have refuge in God. Then what can anyone else do to you!” Swamishri infused strength and self-confidence in the aspirant and emphasized the power of refuge in God.

ds.t: Thinking happiness lies elsewhere is ignorance
w: In the evening, once the walking machine was set up in his room, Swamishri came to walk. The doctors were watching closely the whole time. After five minutes, to find out whether Swamishri was out of breath, Yogicharan Swami said, "Please say a long sentence."

Swamishri looked at him for a moment and, smiling gently, said, "There is no happiness anywhere like the happiness of worshipping God. Thinking that happiness lies elsewhere is ignorance." Even in an ordinary sentence, Swamishri's inner feeling and love shone through.

Every moment of Swamishri is dedicated to satsang. Even during his personal routines, he keeps listening to spiritual scriptures or satsang literature. Even while walking on the treadmill, Swamishri keeps receiving reports of satsang activities, or listening to new satsang publications. In this way Swamishri uses every moment for satsang. Carrying the responsibility of such a vast organisation, he never seems weighed down in any activity; he always seems light.
Today too the walk on the treadmill was going on. During conversation, when Amityash Swami described the layout of Nadiad, Swamishri, linking it to an old rhyme, spoke up:
'The town of Nadiad has nine gates.
At each gate, nine banyan trees.
On each banyan tree, nine branches.
On each branch, nine hanging pots.
In each pot, nine sers of ghee.
Tell me! How much ghee is that?'
Having travelled through many villages over many years, Swamishri has a deep knowledge of the character, the picture and the nature of each village.

Swamishri had returned from touring outside. In the inner room, preparations for EECP treatment had been made. When Swamishri is in Gujarat, Dr. Bajdiya and Dr. Amrutbhai come from Ahmedabad for this treatment. Seeing them here again today, Swamishri immediately asked, "Have all these people been given breakfast or not?"
Vedpurush Swami said, "Yes, it is done."
"When we came from Nadiad, the police (escort) came with us. Give them breakfast too." Giving this instruction to Vedpurush Swami, Swamishri went into the room for treatment.
While everyone worries about Swamishri's treatment, Swamishri keeps worrying about everyone.

ds.t: Packing up in the middle of the night
w: Swamishri was to stay a few days in Mandvadi village at the Madhubhan Resort. For Swamishri's stay here, the village had been named 'Durgapur' and its lanes 'Manek Chowk'. Swamishri's residence was named 'Akshar Kutir' and Harikrishna Maharaj's residence 'Akshar Ordi'.
When Swamishri entered 'Akshar Kutir', darkness had already fallen.
Prayasvinbhai said, "Today your holy feet have come, and this resort will receive your divine rays, so our complex will shine four times brighter."

In 'Akshar Kutir' Swamishri sat to offer food to Thakorji. Apart from one or two sadhus, no one was there for darshan. 'Swamini Vato' was read, and when it came to being suddenly made to pack up and leave, Swamishri explained: "In earlier times farmers had no right to the land. All land was said to belong to the king. The poor farmer would toil, but if he fell foul of the king, he would be made to pack up in the middle of the night, with cart and bullocks. Cots, pots and pans, whatever he had, he had to take and leave. The poor man would be asleep at night and in the morning he would be made to go. This worldly life is just like that."
Finally, he said to Tyagratna Swami, sitting in front, "If any confusion comes, sit down with this (Swamini Vato)."
Tyagratna Swami said, "Or come here to you."
Swamishri said, "Whether you can come or not, there should be no confusion."
